Hi Tom — thanks for the diagram and the quick summary. I've converted our onboarding checklist into a "connectivity passport" (attached: connectivity-passport-template.pdf) so we have a single artifact to validate during the runbook walk. Below are the concrete items we need from Greenline to clear the environment validation gate. Please fill or confirm each item and return to this thread.

Minimum network & account prerequisites (what we need from you):
- Public egress / NAT: confirm whether you'll whitelist Redwood egress IPs or prefer mutual TLS + dynamic egress (we support both). If static, provide CIDRs or individual IPs.
- DNS/SNI: list any outbound domains that will be inspected by your proxy or require TLS passthrough.
- KMS: confirm BYOK (KMS ARN) or opt for Redwood-managed. If BYOK, please provide KMS key ARN and grant the service principal we will provide.
- Private endpoints: request a list of internal S3 or object-store endpoints, and whether AWS VPC endpoints are required.
- Ports & protocols: confirm ability to allow inbound ports 22/443 to the bastion, and allow outbound 443 to model registries and telemetry endpoints. Detailed port table attached in template.
- Jump host: will you provide a bastion/jumphost or should Redwood provision a managed access proxy? If you provide, list bastion public IPs and allowed admin users.
- Service accounts & IAM: create a read-only service account for deployment validation with the following permissions (IAM list included in the PDF).
- Audit/log delivery: preferred log ingestion (S3 bucket ARN / Syslog endpoint) and expected retention (days).

Operational items and timeline
- Validation window: please propose 2-hour windows next week (we prefer PST mornings).
- Contact: security@greenline.health for SOC/SIEM questions, netops@greenline.health for connectivity work.

I'll copy Rishi and Dev to pick up port-level and runtime questions. Once you return the passport, we'll schedule a live validation session and sign the go/no-go checklist.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 10:03 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll copy Rishi and Dev to pick up port-level and runtime questions. Once you return the passport, we'll schedule a live validation session and sign the go/no-go checklist.

Quick clarifications from the runtime side so the passport can be filled accurately:
- Ports: The runtime requires outbound 443 to our model registry endpoints (model-registry.redwood.ai:443) and to artifact storage (we'll accept S3 or an S3-compatible endpoint). For large model pulls during warmup we may use chunked HTTPS range requests.
- Health checks: Liveness/readiness endpoints are over HTTP on port 8080 internally. We don't require inbound 8080 on public NAT — those stay inside the VPC.
- KV cache & control plane: control-plane callbacks (for metrics/trace) will connect to telemetry.redwood.ai:443. If your environment restricts egress, please whitelist that FQDN or the IP range we list in the passport.
- Bastion: If you provide a bastion, we need an account/user we can SSH as for the validation window (key-based). If you want Redwood-managed access, we can provide a temporary CA cert and ephemeral user (preferred for orgs with strict IAM).

I'll add a short table with the exact domains/IPs to the passport and resend.

-Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
